name: Coldridge Valley Mail Delivery
summary: At Anvilmar, Coldridge Valley Mail Delivery carries news to scouts beyond the frozen lake. Snow and nearby troggs can leave the valley's defenders cut off, so correspondence keeps them connected.

sections.title: A Courier in the Snow
sections.body: In Coldridge Valley, news from the rest of Dun Morogh reaches Anvilmar by mountain pass. Winter couriers bring the mail, and the letters soon gather in the hall. Sten Stoutarm manages supplies and security, so he depends on recruits to carry the bundles down the western road. Without them, important messages would remain at Anvilmar.

sections.title: Frontier Outposts
sections.body: Talin Keeneye watches the frozen lake to the west, keeping an eye on trogg movements and dangerous wildlife. Even at a cold outpost, news from Ironforge and the surrounding camps matters. The mountain conditions make sorting mail difficult, and letters for different scouts can end up together in one bundle.

aliases: who gives coldridge valley mail delivery
faq.answer: Sten Stoutarm gives you the delivery outside Anvilmar. Letters have just arrived through the mountain pass, but he is occupied with his duties and cannot carry them himself.
Talin Keeneye is camped west of Anvilmar, beside the road near the frozen lake in Coldridge Valley.

faq.q: Are all the letters in the stack actually for Talin?
aliases: is the mail all for talin
faq.answer: No. Talin finds a letter for Grelin Whitebeard, who is stationed nearby in the valley.

faq.q: Why does Sten need an adventurer to run the mail?
faq.answer: Trogg incursions and local threats keep Sten and the other dwarven defenders busy with supply and security duties. Travelers and recruits can carry letters to the outlying posts.

faq.q: Does this quest lead to other tasks?
faq.answer: Yes. After the delivery, Talin asks you to take the misdirected letter to Grelin Whitebeard, continuing the mail deliveries.

faq.q: Where did the letters originally come from?
faq.answer: The letters came through the pass into Coldridge Valley, from the broader lands of Dun Morogh and Ironforge.

angles.text: As a dwarf, carrying news between outposts helps keep Ironforge's far-flung valley scouts connected to their clans.
As a gnome living among allies in Dun Morogh after Gnomeregan's fall, helping carry messages builds trust with local dwarven defenders.
As an Alliance member, you help keep Coldridge Valley's outposts connected, which matters for coordinating Dun Morogh's defense.
